The claim for compensation raised in this petition is in respect of fatal injuries alleged to have been sustained by the deceased Sh. Santosh Kumar in a motor accident that took place on Archana Kumari vs Sushil Kumar on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36638780/
1 03.08.2015, at about 3.35 pm, at Vandematram Marg, Near Bhuli Bhatiyari Bus Stop, New Delhi,
regarding which one FIR No.263/15, under Sections 279/304-A IPC was registered at PS Mandir Marg.

The vehicle involved in this case is a Wagon R car bearing registration No. UP-14BP-7349,
which at the relevant time of accident was being driven and owned by respondent no. 1 (R-1) and insured with respondent no. 2 (R-2).
2.
As per record, the petitioners are wife, children and mother of the deceased.

Succinctly put, facts of case are that on the above said date and time, the deceased was going from North Avenue to Karol Bagh and was sitting on the back seat of the Wagon R car, which was being driven by respondent no.
1 in rash and negligent manner and at very high speed.

When they reached ahead of Asaram Bapu Ashram on Ridge Road at Vandematram Marg near Bhuli Bhatiyari bus stand, one person was crossing the road and the respondent no. 1 had applied sudden brakes due to which he could not control his car and the car turned turtle and dragged on the road and they sustained injuries.
It is further stated that the deceased was removed to Dr. RML Hospital where his MLC was prepared.
3. Respondent no. 1 has filed its written statement wherein it is stated that he was holding a valid and effective driving license at the MACP No. 213/16 Archana Kumari & Ors.

Anr.

It is further stated that no accident took place with the alleged offending vehicle and the petitioners have falsely implicated the respondents in the present matter.
5. On 13.01.2016, the following issues were framed by this tribunal:-

1 . Whether the injured sustained fatal injuries in the accident which occurred on 03.08.2015 at about 15.35 hrs, Vandematram Marg, Near Bhuli Bhatiyari Bus Stop,
New Delhi, caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. UP-14BP-7349 being driven and owned by respondent no. 1 and insured with respondent no. 2 ?

OPP 3.Relief.

It is pertinent to mention that respondent no. 1 was already proceeded ex-parte vide order dated 01.08.2023.

New Delhi, caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. UP-14BP-7349 being driven and owned by respondent no. 1 and insured with respondent no. 2 ? OPP.
7.
Onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioners.
The first question that needs to be decided is whether the accident was caused by vehicle bearing registration No. UP-14BP-7349.

In order to prove the same, petitioners have examined Retired SI Tulsi Ram as PW4 who deposed that on 03.08.2015, he was posted at PS Mandir Marg for emergency duty and received a call vide DD No.
20A at around 03.35 pm regarding the occurrence of accident at Vande Matram Marg, opposite Bhuli Batyari, Delhi.

He further deposed that one Wagon R car bearing registration No.
UP-14BP-7349 was found in accidental condition.

Thereafter, he went to Dr. RML Hospital where the MLCs of Sushil Kumar and Santosh Kumar were prepared, which are Ex. PW4/A and Ex.
PW4/B and the deceased was found unfit for giving his statement.
Thereafter, he again reached at the spot of accident and seized the Wagon R car vide seizure memo Ex. PW4/C and prepared rukka and site plan of the spot of accident as Ex. PW4/E.
He also sent Constable Mandeep to PS Mandir Marg for registration of FIR, which is Ex. PW4/D.
He had also recorded the statement of eye witness Sh. Ashok Kumar as Ex. PW4/F.

He further deposed that Sh. Santosh Kumar was declared dead by the doctors on 09.08.2015 and the postmortem report of deceased is Ex. PW4/G.
8.

During cross examination, he deposed that there was smell of breath as alcoholic mentioned in the MLC of Sushil, but he did not obtain MACP No. 213/16 Archana Kumari & Ors. Vs. Sushil Kumar & Anr. Page No. 4 of 19 the sample of Sushil.

sentences.text: However, he admitted that there is a duty constable present at each and every hospital and it is mandatory to collect the sample of person who is under the state of intoxication and thereafter the sample has to be properly packed and sent to the FSL for further investigation.
He further deposed that after due investigation, the case file was handed over to the MACT cell, Mandir Marg and the same was assigned to ASI Vijay Pal for further investigation.
Admittedly, there is no medical examination of respondent no. 1 in order to ascertain the quantity of alcohol in his blood at the relevant time.
Section 185 of the Motor Vehicle Act provides that a person is liable to be punished if he founds under the influence of alcohol exceeding 30mg/100 ml of blood.
In the instant case, there is no evidence on record to prove that the respondent no. 1 had consumed alcohol exceeding the prescribed limit at the relevant time.

9. The petitioners have further examined on record Retired SI Vijay Pal Singh as PW5 who deposed that he was second Investigating Officer of the present matter and received the case file for further investigation.
He deposed that he had arrested Sushil Kumar at the instance of eye witness Ashok vide arrested memo Ex. PW5/B and also seized his driving license vide seizure memo Ex. PW5/C.
He further deposed that he had recorded the supplementary statement of eye witness Ashok Kumar on 14.08.2015 as Ex. PW5/D and thereafter again on 17.08.2015 as Ex. PW5/E.

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as is required in a criminal prosecution.

Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as (2009) 13 SC 530 in case titled Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein it has been observed that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to for the claimants and the claimants were required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.

sentences.text: The compensation to which the petitioners are entitled shall be under the heads as discussed hereinafter.
(I) Medical or Treatment Expenses 17.

The petitioner no.1/wife of deceased has stepped into the witness as PW2 who tendered her evidence by way of her affidavit Ex. PW2/A and placed on record original medical bills of her deceased husband as Ex. PW2/27 (colly) which are totalling to a sum of Rs. 3,664/-
18.
Respondents have not led any evidence to show that the said bills do not relate to the injuries suffered by the deceased in the aforesaid accident.
Thus, the testimony of PW-2 regarding medical bills of her deceased husband remained unrebutted and uncontroverted.
In the absence of any plausible evidence produced by respondents on record, there is no reason to disbelieve the testimony of PW-2 regarding medical bills of her deceased husband.
Hence, the petitioners are entitled to Rs.3,664/- towards medical expenses of the deceased.

The petitioner no.1/wife of deceased has stepped into the witness as PW2 who tendered her evidence by way of her affidavit Ex. PW2/A wherein she deposed that her deceased husband was B.A. Hons and was working as UDC in DPR under Ministry of Defence - JS(TRG) & CAO, E Block,

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In the instant case, there is no evidence on record to prove that the respondent no. 1 had consumed alcohol exceeding the prescribed limit at the relevant time.
Reliance has been placed upon the judgments in cases National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs.
Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287 and United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Deepak Goel and Ors., 2014 (2) TAC 846 (Del.) decided by the Coordinate Bench of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court, wherein it was held that "......where the claimants filed either the certified copies of the criminal record or the criminal record showing the completion of MACP No. 213/16 Archana Kumari & Ors. Vs. Sushil Kumar & Anr. Page No. 5 of 19 investigation by police or issuance of charge sheet under Section 279/304A IPC or the certified copy of FIR or the recovery of the mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle, then these documents are sufficient proof to reach to a conclusion that the driver was negligent particularly when there is no defence available from the side of driver."
11. Reliance has also been placed upon the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Meera Devi & ors., 2021 LawSuit (Del) 2021 wherein it was held that "......in view of Delhi Motor Accident Claim Tribunal Rules, 2008, contents of DAR has to be presumed to be correct and read in evidence without formal proof of the same unless proof to the contrary was produced."
Therefore,
an adverse inference is drawn against the respondent no. 1/driver in terms of judgment MACP No.
213/16 Archana Kumari & Ors.
reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.
14.
It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as is required in a criminal prosecution.
16. As rashness and negligence on part of driver of the offending vehicle/respondent no. 1 has been proved, the petitioners have become entitled to compensation for death of their family member in the said MACP No. 213/16 Archana Kumari & Ors. Vs. Sushil Kumar & Anr. Page No. 7 of 19 accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
Respondents have not led any evidence to show that the said bills do not relate to the injuries suffered by the deceased in the aforesaid accident.
Thus, the testimony of PW-2 regarding medical bills of her deceased husband remained unrebutted and uncontroverted.
In the absence of any plausible evidence produced by respondents on record, there is no reason to disbelieve the testimony of PW-2 regarding medical bills of her deceased husband.
Hence, the petitioners are entitled to Rs.3,664/- towards medical expenses of the deceased.
It is explicit from the testimonies of PW1 and PW3 coupled with the aforesaid exhibited documents that the deceased was working on the post of UDC with Ministry of Defence and was getting the salary of Rs. 24,900/- per month.
Further, the deceased is entitled to 30% of his basic pay towards house rent allowance and also entitled to children education allowance @ Rs. 12,000/-
per annum for two children.
Accordingly, in terms of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs.
Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr., (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been approved by a Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National MACP No. 213/16 Archana Kumari & Ors
Page No. 10 of 19 Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors., (2017)
Archana Kumari vs Sushil Kumar on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36638780/
6 16 SCC 680, the multiplier of '16' is applicable in the present case.
Accordingly, in terms of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (Supra)
and National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. (Supra), 1/4th earning of the deceased shall be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
29. Pertinently, the Hon'ble Apex Court has also held in National MACP No. 213/16 Archana Kumari & Ors. Vs. Sushil Kumar & Anr. Page No. 11 of 19 Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi (Supra)
that compensation awarded under the conventional heads shall be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years and a period of 3 years have already elapsed since the deceased had expired.
Hence, the petitioners in this case are also entitled to an increase @ 10% on the amount awarded under the conventional head of 'loss of estate', 'funeral charges' and 'loss of consortium'.
